findings.reason: The authentic standalone original tile contains no diagram. A concrete picture materially clarifies the reversed rectangle gluing, the single sphere-bundle boundary, and the distinction between the complementary disk and the Mobius band. The complete existing proof does not remove this explanatory benefit.

diagram_math_checks.data: Left rectangle [0,1] x [-1,1] with opposite vertical edge arrows, blue top and bottom, dashed t=0.
diagram_math_checks.checks: The Given relation (0,t)~(1,-t) maps the upward left-side direction to the downward right-side direction. It joins the two horizontal fiber-end edges into one boundary circle S(L); t=0 is the zero section. No top/bottom identification is drawn.

diagram_math_checks.data: Middle projective-disk model: antipodal outer boundary points, blue inner disk D^2, surrounding annulus D(L), inner boundary S(L).
diagram_math_checks.checks: The two marked opposite outer points illustrate x~-x on the whole outer circle. The inner disk is complementary to the annulus, not the zero section. After the outer antipodal identification, the annulus is the Mobius band and its remaining inner circle is its sphere boundary. D(L) and D^2 meet along S(L).

diagram_math_checks.data: Rightward arrow labelled collapse D^2 then rescale; target projective disk retains the outer antipodal identification and has center basepoint.
diagram_math_checks.checks: The illustrated map is the composite RP^2 -> RP^2/D^2 -> RP^2: first the quotient q collapsing precisely the complementary disk; second the radial homeomorphism of step 2.1. The collapsed disk maps to the displayed center. Since the disk collapse is inside the projective disk, the antipodal outer relation persists. The quotient agrees with D(L)/S(L)=Th(L). No arrow is asserted from the rectangle directly to a filled projective disk.
diagram_math_checks.local_justification: Verification steps 1.1 and 2.1; [F1] Thom quotient convention.
